data.narrative:
Viken Detection, a Series C-stage defense and security company that has raised $50M to date, is evaluated against a comparable universe of 12 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage peers spanning 2 public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms including Helsing, Saronic, Quantum-Systems, Anduril, and Shield AI.

Two valuation methods triangulate on Viken's worth. Stage-progression methodology, applying a typical 1.7x Series C step-up multiplier to the $50M total raised proxy, yields $85M. Peer-median analysis across the 12-company comparable set produces $1.8B, derived from a range spanning $300M (floor) to $18.0B (ceiling, Helsing at Series D). The peer median reflects material dispersion: Quantum-Systems trades at $8.0B (Series C equivalent stage), while earlier-stage Dream Security values at $3.0B.

Triangulation across both methods supports a valuation range of $72M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $930M. The wide dispersion—spanning three orders of magnitude—reflects genuine uncertainty in applying public market and late-stage private comps to an earlier-stage frontier-tech asset. Key sensitivities include Viken's differentiated technology position relative to better-funded peers, near-term revenue visibility, and whether the peer set's elevated valuations reflect sustainable defensibility or sector-wide froth. The stage-progression method alone suggests material upside from current implied fair value.
